newsitem.title: USA: WB Network says five affiliates defect from UPN.
newsitem.headline: WB Network says five affiliates defect from UPN.

text.p: Five television stations affiliated with United Paramount Network have agreed to switch to The WB Television Network owned by Time Warner Inc. next year in a deal worth up to $84 million, The WB said Monday.
The five stations, owned or programmed by Sinclair Broadcast Group Inc., are WPTT-TV in Pittsburgh, WNUV-TV in Baltimore, WSTR-TV in Cincinnati, KRRT-TV in San Antonio and KOCB-TV in Oklahoma City.
The stations will become primary affiliates of The WB for 10 years, starting in January.
The WB and the United Paramount Network launched their networks in late 1994 and early 1995, respectively, in an effort to form a fifth U.S. television network.

The WB guaranteed that Sinclair will receive $64 million in compensation for the switch for the first eight years of the agreement, Baltimore-based Sinclair said in a statement. The network could pay Sinclair anotherr $20 million over the final two years of the deal, but has no obligation to do so.
In addition, Sinclair's stations in Milwaukee and Birmingham and Tuscaloosa, Ala., have extended their affiliations with The WB through January 2008. Glencairn Ltd. owns the station in Milwaukee.
In addition, Sinclair's station in Greenville, S.C., WFBC-TV, will become an affiliate of The WB in November 1999. WFBC-TV is owned by River City Broadcasting LP.
United Paramount Network is owned by Viacom Inc. and BHC Communications Inc., a 76 percent-owned unit of Chris-Craft Industries Inc.

Sinclair Broadcasting stock rose 12.5 cents to $29.50 on Nasdaq. Time Warner slipped 87.5 cents to $45.375 on the New York Stock Exchange. Viacom fell $1.19 to $28.75 on the and BHC Communications rose $1.50 to $123.25, both on the American Stock Exchange.
